title: What a number leaves out
paragraphs: A library judged its success by visitor numbers. Yet a crowded building did not necessarily mean that readers found what they needed.
Staff proposed recording whether questions were answered, alongside attendance. This would not eliminate uncertainty, but might reveal aspects obscured by the headline figure.
The proposal challenged neither measurement itself nor its usefulness; it questioned the assumption that one measure could stand for the whole.
